title: 'Loud Working' Is the New Workplace Trend
paragraphs: Over the last few years, "quiet quitting" became a popular workplace trend. Employees did the work they were paid to do, but stopped doing anything extra like staying late or checking work emails at home.
But now, some employees are doing the opposite. Instead of being "quiet," they're being "loud" about their work, making sure other people notice what they do.
Known as "loud working," this trend is one in which employees try very hard to show they're useful to their company.

It's happening at a difficult time for many workers. People are worried about losing their jobs to layoffs or new AI technology, and in many places, finding a new job has become harder than it was before.
So some workers hope that being more visible will help them keep their jobs, or even get promotions.
Loud working can take different forms. People might talk more about their achievements or try to take on other people's work.

Some may also choose what they do at work more carefully. For example, they might focus on a problem their manager really wants to solve, rather than other work that gets less attention. By solving the big problem, they can show their manager how useful they are and make their work easier to notice.
But loud working becomes a problem when getting noticed becomes more important than doing good work, or working well with others.

When employees feel they need to show how useful they are, they may start competing for attention. "Loud workers" might talk too much in meetings or take credit for work done by a team. And other workers may get frustrated as they are left with all the work that doesn't get as much attention.
So being "loud" may help you at work — but making noise alone isn't enough!
